spec.description: The state stream of the domain-advances brief, steps 2 and 3. The frozen claim examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/claims/protected-age-not-mutated.json, unchanged (DataBinder.bind of one property value named field with the value "32" onto a fresh ProtectedBean, age protected by one disallowed pattern, leaves age 0, for every simple name of at most 8 units), run by examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/proofs/prove.py at its own bound 8 (unwind 16, strict gaps, the ArrayList, ArrayDeque and HashSet models, PropertyEditorRegistrySupport's initializer observed). New since job 20261117-130335: the run takes a stand-in for the bean wrapper's write of a property value (prove --stand-in, lib/src/stand_in.rs; examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/proofs/stand-ins/org/springframework/beans/ProtectedBeanStandIn.java), sampled against the release's own AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor.setPropertyValue(PropertyValue) on a JVM before the run (463,616 samples, all the same), so the introspection caches are off the path; the ArrayList model keeps remove(Object) (checkAllowedFields drops a disallowed value with it); and Boolean.TRUE and Boolean.FALSE are one object each. A capped inline probe at bound 8 refuted vulnerable-protected-state-mutation in 63 s at ageAfterBinding(upperCasePattern=false, field="Age"), which returns 32 on a JVM (the witness is run on a JVM, where the method runs as written, so the refutation rests on no stand-in or model): this job's outcome and evidence.json are what examples/tools/accept.py reads to accept it. The fixed task is expected to stop with no verdict at String.toLowerCase() on a non-ASCII field (DataBinder.isAllowed:828: the frozen claim does not restrict field to ASCII and the checker lowers ASCII only), which this job records as the current blocker.
